text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The man credited with discovering gold in Australia, EDWARD HARGRAVES, was born in 1816.

German/Australian prospector CHARLES RASP, who claimed Broken Hill, was born in 1846. He went inland seeking a dry climate for his lung problems. He claimed Broken Hill, thinking it was a tin deposit, but it turned out to contain silver.
Australian pioneer film director CHARLES CHAUVEL was born in 1897. His films included "In The Wake Of The Bounty", "Forty-thousand Horsemen", "The Rats Of Tobruk" and "Jedda".
German head of the Gestapo HEINRICH HIMMLER was born in 1900. From 1929 he was Hitler's second-in-command.
Former Australian Governor-General Sir ZELMAN COWAN was born in 1919.

American actress JUNE ALLYSON was born in 1923. She was a star of stage and screen and appeared in the film "Best Foot Forward" and in numerous musicals such as "Two Girls And A Sailor" and "The Glenn Miller Story".

American singer and actor AL MARTINO (ALFRED CINI) was born in 1927. His first hit was a million seller in 1952 "Here In My Heart". Other hits included "I Love You Because" (1963), "I Love You More And More Every Day" (1964), "Spanish Eyes" (1965) and "To The Door Of The Sun" (1974). He played the part of Johnny Fontane in "The Godfather"(1972).
South African archbishop of Cape Town Reverend DESMOND TUTU was born in 1931. He was general secretary of the South African Council of Churches and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984.
Award-winning Australian author THOMAS KENEALLY was born in 1935.

United States singer, songwriter and producer JOHN COUGAR MELLENCAMP was born in 1951. He formed his first band at the age of 14 and released his first solo record in 1976. He gained fame and fortune in the 1980's with hits such as "Hurts So Good", "Jack And Diane", "Small Town", "Rock in the USA", "Paper In Fire" and "Cherry Bomb".
British ice-skating champion JAYNE TORVILLE was born in 1957. With partner CHRISTOPHER DEAN, they dominated the sport of ice-skating in the mid-1980's.
** EVENTS **
1858 : A non-stop mail coach reached Los Angeles 20 days
after leaving St Louis. It had covered 4,160 kilometres.
1919 : The first national airline, KLM of Holland, was
established.
1922 : The first royal broadcast was made on British
radio by the Prince of Wales, PRINCE CHARLES.
1937 : Australian exports of hides, butter and lamb were
hit by new import restrictions imposed by Japan.
1938 : Jews in Nazi Germany were ordered to hand in their
passports and within the month hundreds were rounded up and expelled to Poland.
1941 : JOHN CURTIN was sworn in as Prime Minister of
Australia. He owed his win to independents who transferred their support to the labor party, as they believed divisions within the coalition government would harm the war effort.
1956 : The man who introduced the process of
deep-freezing food, died. CLARENCE BIRDSEYE revolutionised eating habits in the western world.
1959 : The first pictures of the far side of the moon
were relayed back to Earth from the Soviet spacecraft Lunik III. 1963 : United States President J.F. KENNEDY signed the Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.
1974 : The first full colour telecast in Australia was
the televising of test patterns in colour. The stations were preparing for the start of programming five months later.
1985 : Italian cruise liner "Achille Lauro" was seized by

Palestinian terrorists. There were 400 passengers on board. The PLO terrorists demanded the release of 50 Arab prisoners in Israeli jails and threatened to blow up the 25,000 ton liner and its passengers. They murdered an elderly and crippled New York Jew named LEON KLINGHOFFER. After lengthy negotiations the terrorist leader Commandant OMAR surrendered on the condition that he and his men were flown to Tunis. Later the Italian government caused a storm of controversy when it released MOHAMMED ABBAS, the man who masterminded the hijacking.
1988 : An Alaskan hunter sparked an international rescue
operation when he spotted grey whales trapped beneath the ice.
1994 : The Federal Government assured Vietnam veterans
that it would consider compensation payments for those exposed to Agent Orange. This followed the Government's formal acknowledgement of a link between the herbicide and cancer.
